messages.subject: Use RAppArmor to knit report in a shiny-app
messages.subject_clean: Use RAppArmor to knit report in a shiny-app
messages.body_plain:
In my app a user can create an rmarkdown report. However, knitting it is a security risk and is disabled on a server. Is it possible to add something like RAppArmor to shinyappsio? https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RAppArmor/index.html

As an example, see the link below (R > Report). When run locally, clicking the 'Knit report' button generates an HTML report.

https://vnijs.shinyapps.io/analytics/?SSUID=bd88dfc0c4

messages.body_plain:
We've had a couple requests <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies/pull/31> for supporting RAppArmor, but we haven't addressed them yet. But that doesn't mean its not something we could support. Out of curiosity, What type of security problems are you trying to avoid using RAppArmor on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>? Applications running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> are already isolated using containers.

messages.body_plain:
I wonder if there is a bug in the rsconnect package.

I am guessing here, but I would try the following, one step at a time and see if they make a difference:

1. Update to the latest version of rsconnect:  devtools::install_github("rstudio/rsconnect"), and try again.
2. Uninstall the openxlsx package and re-install it, and try again.
3. Upgrade devtools , and repeat steps #1 and #2.

messages.body_plain:
If a user knits a report they can execute arbitrary R-code. By using containers you avoid that a user could crash a server but they could still crash a an app that other users are working with. For example, in my app there is a sessions list in the global environment and I'd want to make sure that a user couldn't (accidentally) delete it.

On Friday, April 1, 2016 at 6:50:32 AM UTC-7, Andy Kipp wrote:
> We've had a couple requests <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps-package-dependencies/pull/31> for supporting RAppArmor, but we haven't addressed them yet. But that doesn't mean its not something we could support. Out of curiosity, What type of security problems are you trying to avoid using RAppArmor on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>? Applications running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> are already isolated using containers.

messages.body_plain:
I think the issue is that you can't use anything that uses Tcl or Tk since they require access to the DISPLAY, and there is no DISPLAY that is available to you since the application is running on the server.  With shiny applications, the display is the browser.
Hope this helps.

messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
I am new to ShinyServer but have an app that Take MP3 files, does some processing, and then displays a table with some info about that MP3. When I run the ShinyApp on my local machine it works great. Then when I try to deploy to ShinyApps.IO or event AWS Shiny Server, it does soon after uploading the file. I cannot figure out what the issue is. Any help is appreciated.

Link to App: https://vclip.shinyapps.io/vclipbasic/

Sample Mp3, Log file and Source Files are attached.

I am wondering if these are because of memory issues.

Emad

messages.body_plain:
This is probably related to startup timeout. If you're loading lots of data outside shinyServer() function or in your global.R, you can get this error if that operation takes longer then 60 seconds. You can adjust the startup timeout in the advance settings page for your application in the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> dashboard.

-Andy

-Tareef

messages.subject: Re: oauth_listener() needs an interactive environment in working with Google Drive, shiny app fails to start on shinyapps.io server
messages.subject_clean: oauth_listener() needs an interactive environment in working with Google Drive, shiny app fails to start on shinyapps.io server
messages.body_plain:
A simple solution:   Tareef from RStudio identified the issue I ran into as inconsistent behavior of the PUBLISH functionality in the RStudio IDE.   If you use rsconnect::deployApp(), the "old" way will work--that is, if you have a valid .httr-oauth file in the working directory, the deployApp function loaded all the bits needed for my legacy shiny app to load to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> server.    So while MarkEdmondson1234's fix will indeed work (and is necessary if you want to continue using the PUBLISH button in RStudio 0.99.892 or 0.99.893), for those of us with legacy shiny apps, avoid PUBLISH until the bug is fixed.

On Thursday, January 8, 2015 at 12:18:26 PM UTC-8, Daniel Buijs wrote:
> I've noticed that there's a limit on the total Deployment size of 100 MB. I fully understand why there has to be some limit, but it's been a bit inconvenient for my app that comes in at 108 MB.
>
> Rather than ask for the limit to be raised (which would be a temporary solution, at best), I thought I'd ask the community if they have any ideas for the following situation:
>
> I'm really new to building Shiny apps and I've only managed to get a handful working so far, but I'm seeing the following pattern in my work:
>
> 1. Grab a large public dataset, clean it, format it, calculate derived meta-data, and then put it into some disk storage format (I've found SQLite particularly useful).
> 2. Build a Shiny app that lets users search, filter and aggregate from the cleaned dataset.
> 3. Provide plots, reports, or links to other resources based on the user-generated subset.
>
> The problem is that the actual Shiny code is tiny, maybe a handful of lines, but in order to let users define their own filters and subsets on the fly, the whole dataset has to be available to the Shiny server. Right now this means tiny ui.R and server.R files and giant database file that pushed me over the 100 MB deployment limit.
>
> I just need read access to the database. I'm not altering anything in it, and the user output is tiny too. Because I'm storing it in a file instead of in memory, it's pretty light on RAM and CPU usage as well.
>
> Does anyone have any alternate schemes or ideas for Shiny apps that fit the general pattern of accessing a large static database that wouldn't take up as much space?
>
> Cheers,
>
> D

<http://stackoverflow.com/questions/36462166/error-deploying-to-shinyapps-bundle-does-not-contain-manifest-file-interactive#>

I've signed up to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and created my first demo app. It works fine on my local machine, but I get an error when I try to deploy it:

Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 179717272 failed: Error parsing manifest: Bundle does not contain manifest file: Interactive Plotting with Manipulate   RStudio Support.URL

Here's my code: In the ui.R

library(shiny)

shinyUI(
      pageWithSidebar( headerPanel("Diabetes prediction"),

      sidebarPanel(
            numericInput("glucose", "Glucose mg/dl", 90, min = 50, max = 200, step = 5),
            submitButton("Submit")
      ),
      mainPanel(
            h3("Results of prediction"),
            h4("You entered"),
            verbatimTextOutput("inputValue"),
            h4("Which resulted in a prediction of"),
            verbatimTextOutput("prediction")
      )
))

In the server.R

library(shiny)

diabetesRisk <- function(glucose) glucose / 200

shinyServer( function(input,output){
      output$inputValue = renderPrint({input$glucose})
      output$prediction = renderPrint({diabetesRisk(input$glucose)})
      }
)

I run R studio with R version 3.2.3 (2015-12-10) on a Windows computer. I installed the Shiny and Shinyapps packages today (2016-04-06).

I'm supprised by the error message, because I don't use Manipulate in my code.

I searched Stack overflow and Google, but this specific error message did not come up.

Can anyone help me?

Aliia,
I think the issue is the installR package.  I don't enough about it but reading about the description for it implies that you would use that to install packages.  With shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> you shouldn't be installing packages directly.  Instead you should load the libraries you are using with a direct library() call.  Shinyapps.io will reconstruct the packages you are using on the server.

Hope this helps

The 100MB limit was raised a while ago to 1GB on the free plan and to 3GB at basic and above plans.  How large is your dataset?

On Saturday, April 9, 2016, Vance Lopez <vance....@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi Daniel,
>

> Vance

> On Thursday, January 8, 2015 at 12:18:26 PM UTC-8, Daniel Buijs wrote:
> > I've noticed that there's a limit on the total Deployment size of 100 MB. I fully understand why there has to be some limit, but it's been a bit inconvenient for my app that comes in at 108 MB.
> >
> > Rather than ask for the limit to be raised (which would be a temporary solution, at best), I thought I'd ask the community if they have any ideas for the following situation:
> >
> > I'm really new to building Shiny apps and I've only managed to get a handful working so far, but I'm seeing the following pattern in my work:
> >
> > 1. Grab a large public dataset, clean it, format it, calculate derived meta-data, and then put it into some disk storage format (I've found SQLite particularly useful).
> > 2. Build a Shiny app that lets users search, filter and aggregate from the cleaned dataset.
> > 3. Provide plots, reports, or links to other resources based on the user-generated subset.
> >
> > The problem is that the actual Shiny code is tiny, maybe a handful of lines, but in order to let users define their own filters and subsets on the fly, the whole dataset has to be available to the Shiny server. Right now this means tiny ui.R and server.R files and giant database file that pushed me over the 100 MB deployment limit.
> >
> > I just need read access to the database. I'm not altering anything in it, and the user output is tiny too. Because I'm storing it in a file instead of in memory, it's pretty light on RAM and CPU usage as well.
> >
> > Does anyone have any alternate schemes or ideas for Shiny apps that fit the general pattern of accessing a large static database that wouldn't take up as much space?
> >
> > Cheers,
> >
> > D

> > > 1. Grab a large public dataset, clean it, format it, calculate derived meta-data, and then put it into some disk storage format (I've found SQLite particularly useful).

> > > 3. Provide plots, reports, or links to other resources based on the user-generated subset.

Hi all,

I have a shiny app using the fread function from the R data.table package.

I am able to run it locally quite easily.
But on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, whenever I set the "dec" argument of the function to anything other than the default, the app crashes.

I thinks it comoes from the fact that the fread function would then modify the system default to the specified decimal point, and change it back when the function finished running.

Has anyone esle had the issue before?

Thank you for your help,
Robin

messages.subject: URLs for Shinyapps now moving out of iframe keeping URL parameters?
messages.subject_clean: URLs for Shinyapps now moving out of iframe keeping URL parameters?
messages.body_plain:
Hi ShinyApps team!

As you may remember from before, I use parameters in the URL query string to aid authentication for Google APIs.  I've noticed that since the move away from iframes, its now hard (impossible?) to clear the parameters by providing a link as Shinyapps seems to copy them over, differing from normal website behaviour.  I think this is shinyapps specific, as a local Shiny server doesn't have the issue.

For example, to reset authentication I used to send a user back to a clean URL mark.shinyapps.io/the_app/ <http://mark.shinyapps.io/the_app/> from a link in the menu.  Now however, if a user is on mark.shinyapps.io/the_app?code=xxxxxxx <http://mark.shinyapps.io/the_app?code=xxxxxxx> any links back (including "/" and "http://mark.shinyapps.io/the_app") still preserve the code=xxxxxx, and in my case this means breaking the authenitcation.

I recall this may have been due to a fix in place due to the iframe, so perhaps that fix could be rolled back again now?

Yours sincerely,
Mark

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Cannot logout of a shinyapps.io app
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Cannot logout of a shinyapps.io app
messages.body_plain:
Is the proper way to logout of a shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> application documented anywhere beyond this thread?
Is this process likely to change in the future (and break what is described in this thread)?
How will changes to the logout process be communicated in the future?

On Tuesday, January 26, 2016 at 1:47:51 PM UTC-6, Andy Kipp wrote:
> We've recently changed the way logging into an application hosted on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> works. This was necessary to improve security. It is now a two step process (Both steps are completed in the popup window, when you click 'Login' for a private app):
>
> 1) You must first authenticate to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service (login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io>). When you do this, we create a session cookie for login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io> (called shinyapps_auth).
>
> 2) Once you've authenticated to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service you can then authenticate to the application itself using your existing session for login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io>. This sets another cookie called (therealshinyapps) for the specific application you are logging into.
>
> As I said, both these steps happen automatically when you click "Login" for a private application. The two login steps are necessary, because these cookies must be distinct between shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> itself, and between applications hosted on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
>
> As Fereshteh mentioned, you can logout of an application by visiting the URL: https://userName.shinyapps.io/appName/__logout__/. When you visit this URL you are in fact logged out the application, but you're still got a session cookie for login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io>, so clicking "Login" will simply authenticate you the application using your existing login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io> session without requiring you to re-enter your password.
>
> Currently the login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io> uses a session cookie so if you close your window it *should* require you to re-authenticate with login.shinyapps.io <http://login.shinyapps.io> the next time you attempt to authenticate to an application. That said, it turns out both Chrome and Firefox keep these session cookies around for longer then they should unless you disable the "feature". See this thread <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/10617954/chrome-doesnt-delete-session-cookies> for more info. Regardless you can always logout of the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> service itself by going to https://login.shinyapps.io/logout after you logout of your application. I have some ideas on how to address this, so its something we can likely fix.
>
> I apologize if this is all bit confusing. We've recently done a lot work to improve the security of private applications, and as is typically the case with additional security, it can create more complexity.
>
> -Andy
>

Thank you
SD

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: Shinyapps authentication
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Re: Shinyapps authentication
messages.body_plain:
Hello Subhash,
To answer your first question, you can absolutely build applications similar to the one described by that article with the Standard plan.

On your second question, I am a little unclear on what the ask is.  With the Standard plan you can invite users to access one or more of your applications.  They would use the same auth information for their user account to access any of the applications you make available to them. If the question is whether you could have just one username/password for all your applications, the answer is that shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>'s auth does require an end user.

Hope this answers the question.
-Tareef

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: Shinyapps authentication
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Re: Shinyapps authentication
messages.body_plain:
A public app doesn't need to have any authentication configured for it.  That is the default behavior.

On Tue, Apr 19, 2016 at 9:58 AM, Subhash Jaini <subhas...@gmail.com> wrote:
> ok, so if I wanted to have a "public" app. I would just put in my application to show when the username is null?
>
> On Tue, Apr 19, 2016 at 8:39 AM, Tareef Kawaf <tar...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > Hello Subhash,
> > To answer your first question, you can absolutely build applications similar to the one described by that article with the Standard plan.
> >
> > On your second question, I am a little unclear on what the ask is.  With the Standard plan you can invite users to access one or more of your applications.  They would use the same auth information for their user account to access any of the applications you make available to them. If the question is whether you could have just one username/password for all your applications, the answer is that shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>'s auth does require an end user.
> >
> > Hope this answers the question.
> > -Tareef
> >

> > > I am also wondering if I can get a centralized username/pass for all the apps :)
> > >

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have 3 questions regarding the deployment of my app which is data intensive.  As follows:

1. I am currently working with the free plan.  Issue I am facing is that sometimes (once in a while not always) I see the message "Disconnected from Server" and I have to refresh the browser to re launch the app.  Is this something that is a server side issue.  Can I expect this issue even if I upgrade to a paid plan?

2. Currently my r calculations are taking ~ 3 seconds in the free plan.  Can I expect better and faster performance on a paid plan. (somewhere ~ 1-1.5 seconds etc).  Speed is critical to my app. I have optimized the code from my end.

3. If my code is optimized and the server performance is super, the only reason behind a poor customer experience could be the end users internet speed.  The way I would like to deal with this situation is to run some logic server end to limit the data depending on the users internet speed.  I have seen such logic being used by JS apps but was wondering if anyone has ever tried to build such a logic with R in shinyapps?

Thank you
Sushanta

Issue I am facing is that sometimes (once in a while not always) I see the message "Disconnected from Server" and I have to refresh the browser to re launch the app.  Is this something that is a server side issue.  Can I expect this issue even if I upgrade to a paid plan?

The disconnected from server message will occur when the R process backing your shiny application is shut down.  That can occur when the idle timeouts are reached (which are configurable in the paid plans), when your application runs out of memory (you can get more memory in the paid plans), or when your application has an uncaught error that crashes the R process (not resolved by any paid plan).   It is hard to know which of these conditions you are facing, but hopefully this information along with the log and tuning articles we have can help you figure it out.

>
> 2. Currently my r calculations are taking ~ 3 seconds in the free plan.  Can I expect better and faster performance on a paid plan. (somewhere ~ 1-1.5 seconds etc).  Speed is critical to my app. I have optimized the code from my end.

Right now there is no cpu performance boost that you would see on the paid plans, I suspect that if an application with a single user has calculations that take 3 seconds, you wouldn't see an improvement on the paid plan.  If you only see the 3 seconds of computation when there are multiple people accessing the application and the normal performance is <2 seconds for a single user then you can scale that linearly with the paid plan.

>
> 3. If my code is optimized and the server performance is super, the only reason behind a poor customer experience could be the end users internet speed.  The way I would like to deal with this situation is to run some logic server end to limit the data depending on the users internet speed.  I have seen such logic being used by JS apps but was wondering if anyone has ever tried to build such a logic with R in shinyapps?

Unless you are doing something special, the logic in shiny applications DOES run on the server already.   Perhaps I am not understanding the ask here.

If the "new logic" detects the end user internet speed to be ~ 120 Mbps, the server.R can load 10 years of data from the database and show the user.  This way the user will have a good customer experience in my webapp.

I was wondering if building such a "end user internet speed" logic is possible in Shiny.  I have seen people try our methods in Java but I was not sure of any one trying this on Shiny

Hope this helps

Thank you
SD

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Shiny Server Paid Plans and Other Queries
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Shiny Server Paid Plans and Other Queries
messages.body_plain:
That sounds like more of a shiny question so I will cc the shiny-discuss list to see if others have opinions on it.
My intuition is that the transfer speed will be less of a concern in most cases than the performance of the application within R itself since you probably won't be sending down all the data to the client anyway.

On Thursday, April 21, 2016, Sushanta Deb <sushant...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Thank you Tareef.  I will try and explain the third one a little further.  It may or may not be relevant to this forum but any help will be appreciated.
>
> When my app launches/initiated by an end user, I would like to have a piece of logic in my server.R/ ui.R that estimates the end users' internet speed based on time to render the initial page and then I can use that metric to pass a logic to my server.R to limit the data in the application.
>
> For example, if end user internet speed measured by the "new logic" that I am looking for above, in a given instance, says ~5 Mbps, the server.R will only show him last 6 months data.  If the "new logic" detects the end user internet speed to be ~ 120 Mbps, the server.R can load 10 years of data from the database and show the user.  This way the user will have a good customer experience in my webapp.
>
> I was wondering if building such a "end user internet speed" logic is possible in Shiny.  I have seen people try our methods in Java but I was not sure of any one trying this on Shiny
>
> Hope this helps
>
> Thank you
> SD
>
>
>
> On Thursday, April 21, 2016 at 3:47:14 PM UTC+2, Tareef Kawaf wrote:
> > Hi Sushanta,
> > Please see my responses below
> >
> > On Thu, Apr 21, 2016 at 4:23 AM, Sushanta Deb <sushant...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Hi,
> > >
> > > I have 3 questions regarding the deployment of my app which is data intensive.  As follows:
> > >
> > > 1. I am currently working with the free plan.  Issue I am facing is that sometimes (once in a while not always) I see the message "Disconnected from Server" and I have to refresh the browser to re launch the app.  Is this something that is a server side issue.  Can I expect this issue even if I upgrade to a paid plan?
> >
> > The disconnected from server message will occur when the R process backing your shiny application is shut down.  That can occur when the idle timeouts are reached (which are configurable in the paid plans), when your application runs out of memory (you can get more memory in the paid plans), or when your application has an uncaught error that crashes the R process (not resolved by any paid plan).   It is hard to know which of these conditions you are facing, but hopefully this information along with the log and tuning articles we have can help you figure it out.
> >
> >
> > >
> > > 2. Currently my r calculations are taking ~ 3 seconds in the free plan.  Can I expect better and faster performance on a paid plan. (somewhere ~ 1-1.5 seconds etc).  Speed is critical to my app. I have optimized the code from my end.
> >
> > Right now there is no cpu performance boost that you would see on the paid plans, I suspect that if an application with a single user has calculations that take 3 seconds, you wouldn't see an improvement on the paid plan.  If you only see the 3 seconds of computation when there are multiple people accessing the application and the normal performance is <2 seconds for a single user then you can scale that linearly with the paid plan.
> >
> > >
> > > 3. If my code is optimized and the server performance is super, the only reason behind a poor customer experience could be the end users internet speed.  The way I would like to deal with this situation is to run some logic server end to limit the data depending on the users internet speed.  I have seen such logic being used by JS apps but was wondering if anyone has ever tried to build such a logic with R in shinyapps?
> >
> > Unless you are doing something special, the logic in shiny applications DOES run on the server already.   Perhaps I am not understanding the ask here.
> >
> >
> > >
> > > Thank you
> > > Sushanta

Hi Andy,

My application works fine locally, and when deployed it gave me application failed to start without any log entry. I tried adjusting the Worker Startup Timeout and still had failed to start. Do you have any suggestions? here it is <https://najla.shinyapps.io/WordPredictions/>

> The other thing you should consider is adjusting the "Worker Startup Timeout" setting. This can be found under the "Advanced" tab on the Settings Page for your application in the dashboard.
>
> I think what may be happening here is that if you are loading or processing a lot of data when the application starts up, you may be hitting the default startup time of 60 seconds. Increasing the "Worker Startup Timeout", may address this. messages.subject: Schema for data pipe to Shiny App
messages.subject_clean: Schema for data pipe to Shiny App
messages.body_plain:
I'm hoping someone will point me in a direction or at least opine in brief.

I know R reasonably well, but not much else, programming/ networking-wise.

The problem:

I have a firm that owns remote devices which near-constantly stream raw data via HTTP POSTs of xml or json.

I want to capture and store this data automatically, to later analyze and monitor it through a shiny dashboard.

My plan:
1- set up virtual machine ("VM") running CentOS
2- install R and MariaDB
3- use Gunicorn as a server to listen for POSTs
4- automatically parse and save the XML to MariaDB using python
5- Using a cron job, have the VM email periodic reports generated by RMarkdown/R on the VM
6- Have an app hosted on my shinayapp.io <http://shinayapp.io> account connect to the vm db to get the data at launch (with dplyr)

I've done #1 <https://support.rstudio.com/hc/requests/1>-2 above, and feel confident I can do #5 <https://support.rstudio.com/hc/requests/5>-6. Steps 3 and 4 are more difficult.

My questions:
- Is the above a reasonable structure? It strikes me as overly complex, and I'm wondering if there's an R solution to eliminate the python and/or Gunicorn steps.

- my data is almost always rectangular, but very long. Should I consider skipping the read/write to maria in favor of just writing to csv's (or the new Feather)?

- given that I'm setting up a VM, should I just set up shiny server open source on the VM, or is this level of knowledge overhead considerably higher?

Thanks for any guidance
